system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the eighth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
[Image: Geometric diagram]

In this diagram, CD = CE.
What is the value of x?

Figure, described in words:
A geometric diagram with two triangles, ABC and CDE, meeting at vertex C.
- Segment BD is a horizontal line containing point C between B and D.
- Segment AE is a straight line that intersects line BD at point C.
- Segment AB is vertical and perpendicular to BD, with a right-angle square mark shown at angle ABC.
- Line segment AB extends slightly above point A.
- Angle BAC is marked with an arc and labeled 50°.
- On triangle CDE, segment CD and segment CE each have a single tick mark indicating CD = CE.
- Segment DE connects points D and E.
- Angle CDE at vertex D is marked with an arc.
- Angle DEC at vertex E is marked with an arc and labeled x°.

A. 40
B. 50
C. 60
D. 70

answer.description: The letter of the option you choose for the question.
answer.title: Answer

llm_thinking:
With right angle at B and angle BAC = 50°, angle ACB works out to 40°. Since B-C-D and A-C-E are straight lines, angle DCE is vertically opposite angle BCA, so it's also 40°, which I can now use in triangle CDE.

Since CD = CE, triangle CDE is isosceles, so the base angles CDE and DEC each equal (180-40)/2 = 70°. That gives x = 70, so the answer is D.
